The menu, your way

What are you craving?

Four counters under one roof. Tap what you're in the mood for.

Snoqualmie Gourmet, scooped to order

Small-batch ice cream from a local Washington creamery, plus dairy-free options — served in a fresh waffle cone or a cup. Ask what's churning today.

  • Cascade Blackberry
  • Yakima Peach
  • Huckleberry
  • Strawberry Cheesecake
  • Kahlua Almond Fudge waffle cone $5.50
  • Dairy-free options

Flavors rotate — this is a taste of what's come through the case.

Made from Peggy's mother's recipes

The fudge, caramels, and peanut brittle come from family recipes passed down through a high-school home-ec class. Hand-dipped chocolates and freeze-dried candy round out the case.

  • Homemade fudge
  • Caramels
  • Habanero caramel for the brave
  • Peanut brittle
  • Hand-dipped chocolates
  • Freeze-dried candy
  • Candy kabobs $3.00
  • Dried-fruit kabobs $3.50

A wall of 100+ loose-leaf teas

The powder-blue tea wall is the shop's quiet showpiece — over a hundred jars to scoop and blend by hand. A few regulars off the shelf:

  • Purple Mountain Majesty
  • Sunset in Seattle
  • Hawaiian Colada
  • Masala Chai
  • Cream Earl Grey
  • Market Spice
  • Blue Mango
  • Thai Chai Ginger
  • Lemongrass

Espresso & a scone, off the awning

The red awning says it plainly — espresso, ice cream, fudge, chocolate & tea. Pull up for a coffee and a house scone mix, or an affogato that pours espresso right over a scoop.

  • Espresso & drip
  • Affogato
  • Scone mixes
  • Local jams

Grab-and-go treats on the counter change with the season.

Est. 2005 in the old Enumclaw National Bank

Our story

Two decades of homemade, in the old Enumclaw bank.

Sweet Necessities opened in July 2005, when Toby and Peggy Wenham turned the ground floor of the historic Enumclaw National Bank building into a candy shop instead of renting it to offices.

The recipes came from home — Peggy's mother and the caramels, fudge, and peanut brittle she learned in high-school home ec. The ice cream came from just up the road, small-batch from a Washington creamery. In 2019, Insider named it the best ice cream shop in the whole state.

Today the Harris family keeps the case full and the tea wall stocked — same corner, same recipes, same reason to walk downtown.

Homemade ice cream, candy & tea on Griffin Ave in downtown Enumclaw. Family-run since 2005.
